description: Baseline, unmodified model.py/train.py: black-box 1-layer LSTM (n_hidden_states=64, hidden_sizes=[64], direct_feedthrough=True), 5-fold phase-grouped CV, 600s/fold budget.
Grey-box PARALLELWH, symmetric branches (n_branches=2, n_taps_h=64, n_taps_s=64, nonlinearity hidden_sizes=[16], Tanh), max_epochs raised to 20000 (FIR conv model trains much faster/epoch than LSTM).

Black-box 1-layer GRU (n_hidden_states=64, hidden_sizes=[64], direct_feedthrough=True), otherwise same config as run01 LSTM. Diverged/collapsed to near-constant prediction (val RMSE ~1.0 = unnormalized variance, best_epoch median 75).

PARALLELWH, larger FIR taps (n_taps_h=128, n_taps_s=128, up from run02's 64/64), same 600s/fold budget. Worse than run02 (0.0731 vs 0.0528) -- likely undertrained given fixed wall-clock budget and ~4x parameters, not an inherent capacity ceiling.

PARALLELWH, asymmetric branches added to model.py (n_taps_h/n_taps_s/hidden_sizes now accept per-branch lists): branch1 n_taps=96/hidden=[24], branch2 n_taps=32/hidden=[8]. Worse than run02's symmetric 64/64 (0.0758 vs 0.0528).
PARALLELWH, deeper/wider nonlinearity MLP (hidden_sizes=[32,32], up from run02's [16]), taps left at 64/64. Worse than run02 (0.0628 vs 0.0528) -- nonlinearity capacity is not the bottleneck either.

Black-box 1-layer vanilla RNN (n_hidden_states=64, hidden_sizes=[64], direct_feedthrough=True, tanh), otherwise same config as run01 LSTM. Diverged (val RMSE ~0.89, best_epoch median 175) -- completes the black-box family sweep (LSTM works, GRU/RNN both diverge on this benchmark).

PARALLELWH, same 128/128 taps as run04 but fold_time_budget_seconds overridden to 1500 (2.5x). Still worse than run02 (0.0662 vs 0.0528) despite median best_epoch rising to 10550 (from run04's 2925) -- confirms 128/128 is a genuine regression, not purely a time-budget artifact.

PARALLELWH with new ParametricIIRBlock front/back filters (filter_type=iir, n_taps=96 kernel length, 3rd-order pole/zero cascade: biquad + first-order section) replacing FIRBlock, lr=1e-3 (unchanged). Collapsed to near-constant prediction from epoch 0 (val RMSE ~1.0, loss non-decreasing/oscillating), best_epoch median 425 -- optimization pathology, not a capacity issue.

Retry of run09's ParametricIIRBlock with lr lowered 10x (1e-4) and early_stopping_patience raised to 15. Loss now decreases monotonically instead of oscillating, but converges smoothly TOWARD the same degenerate constant-output solution (val RMSE 1.0198->0.9997 over 650 epochs, plateaus there) -- confirms a structural collapse (likely pole-radius sigmoid saturating toward 0, killing its own gradient) rather than a learning-rate issue. Abandoning ParametricIIRBlock/filter_type=iir.

PARALLELWH, n_branches=3 (up from run02's true-to-physical 2), same per-branch sizing (64/64 taps, hidden_sizes=[16]). First improvement since run02: 0.051911 vs 0.052832 (~1.7%). Test RMSEs also improved at every amplitude level vs run02.

PARALLELWH, n_branches=4 (up from run11's 3). Further improvement: 0.050218 vs run11's 0.051911. Branch-count increase continues to help, unlike taps/MLP-width increases (run04/run06/run08), which all hurt -- an extra branch acts differently from more capacity within existing branches.
PARALLELWH, n_branches=6 (up from run12's 4). Worse than run12 (0.0516 vs 0.0502) -- the branch-count trend plateaus/reverses somewhere between 4 and 6.

PARALLELWH n_branches=4 (run12's config) + new zero-initialized black-box GRU residual-correction path (residual_hidden_size=16) added to model.py, summed on top of the branch outputs. Diverged despite zero-init (val RMSE 0.1421, best_epoch median only 75) -- confirms GRU components are broadly unstable on this benchmark's optimization landscape (run03/run07 standalone, now also as a residual). Abandoning the GRU-residual hybrid idea.

PARALLELWH, n_branches=5 (between run12's 4 and run13's 6). Worse than run12 (0.0534 vs 0.0502) -- confirms the branch-count sweep peaks at exactly n_branches=4 (run11=3: 0.0519, run12=4: 0.0502, run15=5: 0.0534, run13=6: 0.0516).

PARALLELWH n_branches=4 (run12's config) + weight_decay=1e-5. Slightly worse than run12 (0.0510 vs 0.0502) -- expected, since train/val RMSE have stayed matched throughout the search (no overfitting to regularize away).

PARALLELWH n_branches=4 (run12's config) + crops_per_step=2 (average training-loss gradient over 2 independently-sampled windows per step instead of 1). New best: 0.048325 vs run12's 0.050218 (~3.8% better). Test RMSEs improved at every amplitude level too.
PARALLELWH n_branches=4, crops_per_step=4 (up from run17's 2). Further improvement: 0.046543 vs run17's 0.048325. Gradient-averaging trend continues.
PARALLELWH n_branches=4, crops_per_step=8 (up from run18's 4). Worse than run18 (0.0478 vs 0.0465) -- crops_per_step trend peaks at exactly 4 (run17=2: 0.0483, run18=4: 0.0465, run19=8: 0.0478).
